name: Review a Poorly Structured QML Application
scenario_description: Review a proposed QML codebase that embeds raw SQLite queries and file parsing directly inside QML JavaScript event handlers.
research_requirements: QML/C++ architectural boundary, separation of concerns, QAbstractListModel, database offload.
expected_behavior: Critique embedding business logic, synchronous database transactions, and data modeling inside QML; explain that running SQLite on the GUI main thread causes UI stuttering and frame drops; instruct moving database queries and data ownership to C++; implement a C++ QAbstractListModel or QObject controller exposed via QML_ELEMENT.
failure_conditions: Approving SQL queries inside QML event handlers
Failing to separate UI presentation from data persistence

name: Design a Qt Quick Application Architecture
scenario_description: Design the CMake build configuration and component structure for a modern Qt 6 Qt Quick application.

input.user_prompt: How do I configure CMake for a modern Qt 6 Qt Quick application with custom C++ models and QML components without using legacy qrc files or qmlRegisterType?

research_requirements: Qt 6 CMake integration, qt_add_qml_module, QML_ELEMENT, QML_SINGLETON, ahead-of-time QML compilation.
expected_behavior: Provide modern Qt 6.5+ CMake configuration using qt_standard_project_setup() and qt_add_qml_module(); explain URI specification (e.g. MyCompany.App) and declaring QML_FILES and SOURCES together; explain how qt_add_qml_module compiles QML to C++ AOT and automatically registers classes marked with QML_ELEMENT and QML_SINGLETON without manual runtime registration.
failure_conditions: Recommending obsolete Qt 5 qmlRegisterType in main.cpp
Generating manual XML .qrc resource files instead of qt_add_qml_module

name: Identify Excessive Business Logic Inside QML
scenario_description: A developer writes an entire REST client and JSON parsing pipeline in QML JavaScript XMLHttpRequest callbacks and asks why the UI freezes during payload parsing.
research_requirements: QML threading, QNetworkAccessManager, QJsonDocument, asynchronous C++ offload.
expected_behavior: Diagnose two severe flaws: 1) Synchronous XMLHttpRequest completely halts the QML scene graph rendering loop; 2) Parsing massive JSON payloads in JavaScript blocks the UI thread for seconds; instruct moving network operations to C++ using QNetworkAccessManager and QJsonDocument; offload parsing to QtConcurrent::run or a worker QThread, emitting signals back to QML upon completion.
failure_conditions: Failing to offload heavy JSON parsing from the GUI thread

name: Diagnose a Broken Property Binding
scenario_description: In a responsive Qt Quick panel, the width binding ceases to respond to window resizing after the user clicks a reset button.
research_requirements: QML property binding lifecycle, imperative assignment destruction, ternary expressions, Binding element, Qt.binding().
expected_behavior: Diagnose that assigning panel.width = 300 imperatively permanently destroys the declarative binding to parent.width * 0.4; explain that future changes to parent.width will no longer update panel.width; prescribe solutions: 1) Use a state variable with a declarative ternary binding (`width: isCustom ? 300 : parent.width * 0.4`); 2) Re-establish the binding programmatically via `panel.width = Qt.binding(() => parent.width * 0.4)` or use a `Binding` item.
failure_conditions: Failing to explain that assigning a value destroys the binding
Blaming parent layout or window resizing

name: Review QML/C++ Integration
scenario_description: A team uses setContextProperty() in main.cpp for 25 different C++ objects and asks why qmllint fails and QML AOT compilation cannot resolve property types.
research_requirements: Modern Qt 6 QML registration, setContextProperty limitations, QML_ELEMENT, QML_SINGLETON, qmllint type safety.
expected_behavior: Explain that setContextProperty() injects dynamically typed untyped globals into the QML root context, which blinds qmllint from verifying types at compile time and prevents qmlcachegen from compiling QML to native C++; prescribe refactoring: mark manager classes with QML_ELEMENT or QML_SINGLETON, export them via qt_add_qml_module, and import them with explicit namespaces in QML files.
failure_conditions: Recommending keeping setContextProperty for all objects
Failing to explain why qmllint cannot resolve context properties

name: Diagnose GUI Thread Blocking
scenario_description: A Qt application window becomes completely unresponsive with 'Application Not Responding' (ANR) / spinning beachball whenever the user generates a cryptographic report.
research_requirements: Qt GUI thread responsiveness, event loop starvation, QThread, moveToThread, QtConcurrent::run, QProgressDialog.
expected_behavior: Diagnose that the tight loop executes on the GUI main thread, starving the QCoreApplication event loop of CPU time and preventing window redraws, input processing, and OS heartbeat replies; explain that updating progressBar->setValue inside the loop does not repaint the screen without event loop processing; prescribe offloading computation to a worker QThread via moveToThread or QtConcurrent::run, reporting progress via queued signals and slots.
failure_conditions: Recommending calling QCoreApplication::processEvents() in the loop as the primary fix
Leaving heavy computation on the GUI thread

name: Evaluate Qt Widgets vs Qt Quick
scenario_description: A scientific team is designing a desktop CAD tool featuring dockable toolbars, thousands of dense spreadsheet cells, nested menus, and traditional desktop controls, and asks whether Qt Widgets or Qt Quick is better suited.

input.requirements: Data-dense desktop application, complex dockable panels, MDI interface, thousands of visible cells, pixel-perfect integration with KDE Breeze desktop theme, accessibility via screen readers.

research_requirements: Qt Widgets vs Qt Quick decision matrix, QMainWindow, QDockWidget, QTableView, QStyle, AT-SPI accessibility.
expected_behavior: Advise choosing Qt Widgets; explain that Qt Widgets is purpose-built for data-dense desktop workstation software with native QMainWindow dockable layouts (QDockWidget), complex menus, mature Model/View virtualization (QTableView with custom QStyledItemDelegate), mature AT-SPI accessibility, and pixel-perfect native desktop styling via QStyle; explain that Qt Quick is optimized for fluid animations and touch/mobile interfaces, making complex dockable MDI desktop tools harder to build and maintain.
failure_conditions: Recommending Qt Quick for a complex dockable desktop CAD tool without evaluating trade-offs
